name: Spider Memory
subject: Biology
headline: A tiny spider may remember who it has met.
hook: A tiny loner spider may remember who it has met.
found: Jumping spiders told a familiar spider from a stranger.
matters: Big social smarts can fit in a very small brain.

name: Babbling Bat
subject: Biology
headline: Baby bats may benefit from more than a song playlist.
hook: Baby bats babble, just like human babies.
found: Pups with more involved mothers practiced longer and sounded more grown-up.
matters: Learning to talk may lean on caring parents in many animals.

name: Tiny Gardener
subject: Biology
headline: A yak’s best friend might be a tiny gardener.
hook: Pika, called pests, may be a yak’s best friend.
found: Yaks gained more weight where some pika lived, because pika clip a poisonous plant.
matters: Wiping out a “pest” can backfire on the animals we care about.

name: Color Number
subject: Psychology
headline: A gray number can make an eye react to color.
hook: For some people, a gray number looks colored.
found: Their pupils reacted to the color they experienced, though the screen stayed gray.
matters: The colors are real enough that the body responds to them.

name: Pattern Listener
subject: Psychology
headline: A newborn’s brain is already listening for the pattern.
hook: Babies just days old already notice sound patterns.
found: Their brains tracked repeats in syllables and in voices, even when the other kept changing.
matters: We may be born with a pattern finder that helps us learn to talk.
